draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Courtallam! Everyone here walks around with a towel, because this little town in the Western Ghats foothills is all about bathing under waterfalls on the Chittar River. People even call the falls a medical spa, thanks to the medicinal smell of the water.
draft.hungryLine: Food here is traditional South Indian, and the famous stop is a parotta stall on the Sengottai to Tenkasi road that's been drawing queues for over 15 years.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Main Falls are just a 4 min walk, near the bus stand, and the Thirukutralam temple is about 8 minutes away. Five Falls is 6 km from the Main Falls and worth the trip.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Get an oil massage, then take a bath at Sittraruvi, the small falls beside the Main Falls, which is very gentle and safe.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Thirukutralam temple is Chitra Sabha, one of the five dance halls of Shiva, alongside Chidambaram, Madurai, Thiruvalangadu and Tirunelveli.

seeFirst.caption: Short walks and a short drive

spots.name: Coutrallam Falls
spots.detail: 4 min walk · The Main Falls, about 130 feet, where you can bathe 24 hours a day

spots.name: Thirukutralam
spots.detail: 8 min walk · Shiva's Chitra Sabha, close to the Main Falls

spots.name: Five Falls
spots.detail: 6 km from the Main Falls · The water splits into five streams as it drops

legends.title: Sage Agastya's hills
legends.body: Courtallam sits in the Agasthiamalai range, named after the sage Agastya. Locals believe he once lived right here in these hills.

tips.title: Come July to September.
tips.body: The falls are in season with the South West monsoon, and the eight-day Saral Vila festival runs in the Tamil month of Adi, July to August.

tips.title: Skip Shenbagadevi at peak season.
tips.body: This upstream falls is a 30 min trek, and entry is restricted at peak times because of flash floods and crowds.

story.title: Agastya's mountain
story.body: The hills around Courtallam belong to the Agasthiamalai range, named for the sage Agastya, who is believed to have lived in the area.

story.title: A hall for Shiva's dance
story.body: Thirukutralam became one of the five Pancha Sabhas of Nataraja, the Chitra Sabha. It's one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams, where Shiva is worshipped as Kutralanathaswamy.

story.title: A tiny town
story.body: The census counted just 2,368 people living in Courtallam. In season, though, the town fills with visitors who come for the Kuttralam experience.

story.title: Poor man's Ooty
story.body: Locals call it the poor man's Ooty, though prices are rising with its popularity. Bathing spots have police and separate areas for women to keep things safe.

food.name: Rahmed Porata stall
food.detail: Piranoor, on the Sengottai to Tenkasi bus route via Ilanji · Also known as the Bilal Border Parotta Shop
